predecessors.name: Old Great Bulgaria
predecessors.text: the part of Kubrat's Bulgars that Kotrag led north to the Volga after 'the newly founded and still unstable state collapsed'

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the whole country, 'part of the Ulus Jochi' from the conquest of 1236-1241

successors.name: Golden Horde
successors.text: the Ulus Jochi, 'later known as the Golden Horde'

ledger.x: Late 9th century: Volga Bulgaria under Khazar overlordship (mirror of khazaria.json /ledger/12).
969: Volga Bulgaria ceases to be a Khazar vassal (mirror of khazaria.json /ledger/14).
1236: the occupation of the south is overtaken by the general contest.
1241: Volga Bulgaria passes to the Mongols.

wars.name: Rus' raids on Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In the 11th century, the country was devastated by several raids by other Rus''; the page gives no years and no territorial result.

wars.name: Yuri II's campaign against Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In 1220, the Grand Duke Yuri II of Vladimir captured Ustiug and besieged the important Bulgar town of Aşlı.'

wars.name: Battle of Samara Bend
wars.outcome: The Bulgars ambushed the Mongol advance guard 'in the later 1223 or in 1224'; the Volga Bulgaria page: 'In September 1223 near Samara an advance guard of Genghis Khan's army' entered the country and was defeated.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: Mongol victory: Bilyar and Bolghar sacked in 1236, the rebellions put down, the land added to the Ulus Jochi.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontier with the Rus' principalities, the Mordvins and the steppe is approximate throughout.
